title: Leftmost Column With a One
description:
You are given an `m x n` row-sorted binary matrix `mat` where every element is `0` or `1`, and every row is sorted in non-decreasing order (all `0`s appear before all `1`s in each row).

Return the 0-indexed column number of the **leftmost** column that contains at least one `1`. If the matrix contains no `1`s at all, return `-1`.
constraints: mat[i][j] is either 0 or 1, and every row is sorted in non-decreasing order.
hints: Start at the top-right corner (r = 0, c = n - 1).
Whenever mat[r][c] == 1, record c as a better answer and step left (c -= 1); whenever mat[r][c] == 0, step down (r += 1) since no earlier column in row r can hold a 1.

examples.explanation: Column 0 has a 1 at row 1, so the leftmost column with a 1 is 0.
Column 1 is the earliest column containing a 1 (at row 0).
The entire matrix consists of zeros, so return -1.
